title: streaming-schema-deferred-coercion-and-tool-safe-calls
author: Ethan Chen
description:
Motivation: Users deploying structured-response schemas in streaming mode hit two practical problems: 1) strict, byte-by-byte JSON schema coercion during streaming makes partial output fragile (streams can error mid-response when tokens close a schema but checks run aggressively), and 2) function/tool calling can be truncated or misrouted when runtime schema enforcement mutates or rejects intermediate token sequences. This change introduces a conservative, backward-compatible approach: deferred coercion during streaming, a deterministic stream-fallback that emits a machine-friendly error block when final validation fails, and a tool-safe call handshake to avoid dropping tool calls when schemas are active.

Summary of changes: Implemented a 'deferred_coercion' pathway so the runtime defers strict type coercion until the response is complete or until a non-stream (final) flush is requested; added a streaming 'finalize' validation pass that either returns the validated/ coerced object or appends a compact validation error envelope to the stream (so client SDKs can detect structured failures without losing the full transcript); introduced 'function_call_safe_mode' which brokers a minimal metadata-only sub-request to registered tool adapters mid-stream to guarantee tool invocation tokens are not lost if post-validation would reject them; extended the OpenAI compatibility layer with schema aliasing and an 'openai_compat_schema_hints' header to preserve legacy shapes and provide better error messages for downstream SDKs.

Behavioral notes and compat: Default behavior is unchanged for non-stream (classic) responses. For streaming responses, the runtime now emits tokens as before but records a lightweight validation trace; on final token, it will try a best-effort coercion and emit either: (a) a single compact success envelope: {"valid":true,"schema_version":"v2"} (in streaming mode this is appended after a control delimiter), or (b) a compact error envelope with machine-friendly error codes and a short human message (e.g., {"valid":false,"errors":["missing.required field 'items'"],"error_code":"SCHEMA_STREAM_FINALIZE_MISSING"}). This ensures clients receive the full stream plus a conclusive validation status.

Tool/function calling: When response_format triggers a function call in streaming mode, the runtime will now perform a two-step emission: the first step streams partial call payloads as event chunks (unchanged), and when the runtime detects a complete call signature it initiates a function_call_safe_mode handshake to the tool adapter (a synchronous 50ms max window configurable via policy). If the function adapter ACKs the call, the call is committed and will not be removed by later schema coercion. If the adapter NACKs or times out, the call is emitted as a non-committed event and a schema validation may later mark it invalid; clients will receive clear error codes distinguishing adapter failure vs schema rejection.

OpenAI compatibility: Added compatibility mappings so legacy OpenAI-style "response_format": {"type":"json_schema","strict":true} is interpreted as strict mode in non-stream cases but maps to deferred_coercion + strict_finalize in streaming to avoid breaking apps that relied on partial streams. Also added schema_aliases so schema keys can annotate alternate names to preserve older contract names without forcing runtime changes.

Implementation highlights: - runtime/streaming/validator.rs: new DeferredCoercionValidator, streaming finalize hook. - runtime/handlers/func_adapter.go: function_call_safe_mode handshake implementation and timeout policy. - api/types/response_format.go: schema_aliases and openai_compat_schema_hints fields + serialization code. - sdk-python: client change to parse appended validation envelope and expose `StreamValidation` object on finalization. - docs: updated structured output guide with migration notes and examples.

Testing and rollout: Unit + integration tests cover happy path, error envelopes, adapter ACK/NACK, and a small randomized fuzz harness for partial-token edge cases. Canary rollout plan: feature flag gated for 7 days on internal tenants, then opt-in for customers (default on for new accounts). We will monitor metrics: stream.finalize.success_rate, stream.finalize.latency_p50/p95, function_call_safe_mode.handshake_latency, and backward-compat error rate for openai-compat clients.

Open questions/TODO: - Add additional telemetry for envelope size and per-schema failure reasons aggregation. - Consider a user-configurable fallback policy to downgrade to legacy raw-output when finalize failure rate exceeds threshold.

review_comments: Priya Malhotra: Good overall design. Two asks: 1) can we keep the finalize envelope size under 2KB by default? 2) add an opt-out flag for customers that want legacy behavior.
Ethan Chen (author): Answered: added envelope compaction step and config flag 'stream.finalize.max_envelope_bytes' (default 2048). Added flag to API surface and docs.
Liam O'Rourke: Concern about the 50ms handshake window for function adapters in high-latency datacenters. Suggest making it adaptive based on region and adapter RTT history.
Ethan Chen: Implemented adaptive handshake timeout with region-based defaults and a per-adapter override. Documented the fallback semantics.
Anika Rao: Please add clear error code map in SDK docs and include example of migration for openai-compat clients.
Ethan Chen: Added error code appendix and migration snippet in docs/howto/structured-output-streaming.md

release_notes: Improved streaming schema handling: deferred coercion with a final validation envelope, safer function/tool calls during streaming (function_call_safe_mode), and OpenAI-compat mappings for schema hints and aliases. Default behavior unchanged for non-stream responses. See structured-output streaming migration guide.
